observations: Single promotional/stock-style image of a black-and-red indoor spinning/fitness bike.

Image is overlaid with marketing icons claiming health benefits (weight loss, better sleep, more energy, improved blood sugar, stronger immune system, lower blood pressure, lower stress, better mood, improved memory).
Watermark text 'ROYALSS STORE' and a faint 'POSTED ON ...' stamp visible across the bike body, suggesting this may be a stock/catalogue photo rather than the actual unit for sale.

Bike has a seat, handlebar with phone/tablet holder, pedals, a resistance knob, and a bottle in a cage; frame shows a numeric code (e.g. '03998') and partial word 'SPORT' printed on it, not a readable brand/model.
Background is a rough outdoor wall and bare ground, inconsistent with a typical home gym setting, reinforcing the stock-photo impression.
No second angle, no close-up of resistance mechanism, pedals, wiring/display, or any sign of wear or defect is shown.

claims.claim: High-quality Spinning Fitness Bike designed for effective home use
claims.evidence: No close-up or condition shots in photo 0 to confirm build quality or that this exact unit is being sold.

claims.claim: Promotes weight loss, better sleep, more energy, improved blood sugar, stronger immune system, lower blood pressure, lower stress, better mood, improved memory
claims.evidence: These are generic health-benefit claims printed as marketing icons in photo 0, not something a photo can confirm or deny.

risks.risk: Photo may be a generic stock/catalogue image rather than the actual bike being sold, so real condition is unknown.
risks.proof: A fresh photo of the actual bike at the seller's location, including any scratches, rust, or missing parts, with today's date or a handwritten note visible.
risks.if_unproven: priced as used/condition-unknown, not as new

risks.risk: Resistance mechanism, pedals, and flywheel bearing may be worn or non-functional.
risks.proof: A short video clip of the pedals turning and the resistance knob being adjusted.

risks.risk: Seat height/handlebar adjustment knobs could be rusted or broken, common on second-hand spin bikes.
risks.proof: Close-up photo of the adjustment knobs and seat post.

risks.risk: Display/phone holder console may be missing a digital meter or be broken.
risks.proof: Close-up photo of the console/holder area.

proof_requests: Please send a current photo of the actual bike you are selling, taken today, from at least two angles, without marketing overlays.
A short video of the pedals turning and the resistance knob being adjusted.
Close-up photos of the seat post, handlebar adjustment, and any digital console.
response.reason: The item can be identified only by type (spinning fitness bike) with its true condition unverified since the sole photo looks like a stock/marketing image, and no comparable listings were provided to anchor a price.
